page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.vgn6i-m16-vws.5xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual server deployed on KVM virtualization within the ecs.vgn6i-vws family. It is equipped with 20 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 10 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Memory capacity is allocated at 92.0 GB of system RAM, providing approximately 4.6 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is delivered by a dedicated NVIDIA T4 GPU featuring 16 GB of video memory. The configuration contains no local instance storage, requiring all persistent storage and root volumes to operate over remote cloud disks, supported by an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile.

Benchmark evaluations reveal a clear distinction between single-threaded and parallel processing capabilities. Single-core performance is limited, with Geekbench single-core recording 929.0 and stress-ng single-core reaching 1105.39, both placing in bottom-tier performance percentiles. Single-threaded tasks such as gzip compression similarly demonstrate constrained throughput at 19.26 GB/sec. However, multi-threaded workloads leverage the 20 vCPUs effectively, yielding an average rating in stress-ng multi-core (14732.17) and Geekbench multi-core (6611.0). Extended instruction sets including AVX-512F and AES assist in specialized math and cryptography execution, reflected in an average PassMark CPU score of 15713.85.

Memory bandwidth benchmarks show steady execution, registering uncached large-block read speeds of 81.06 GB/sec and write speeds of 49.22 GB/sec. Operational throughput benchmarks align with standard infrastructure requirements, achieving 14.5 million Redis SET operations per second and 11.53 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The ecs.vgn6i-m16-vws.5xlarge presents a balanced cost-efficiency profile for organizations needing dedicated graphics and compute offloading without committing to enterprise-scale training accelerators. The tradeoff lies in its older Intel Skylake-generation architecture and low single-core speeds alongside the absence of local NVMe storage. As a result, this instance is suited for GPU-assisted visualization, virtual workstations, mid-range computer vision inference, 3D rendering pipelines, and general parallel processing workloads relying on network storage.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.vgn6i-m16-vws.5xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine designed for visualization and inference workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture using KVM virtualization, it features 20 dedicated vCPUs from a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processor, 92.0 GB of system memory, and a dedicated NVIDIA T4 GPU with 16 GB of VRAM. It includes no bundled local storage and connects with an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks indicate weak single-core processing metrics, such as a Geekbench single-core score of 929.0 and bottom-quartile compression throughput, countered by balanced multi-threaded execution with a Geekbench multi-core result of 6611.0. Given the pairing of 16 GB GPU memory with 92 GB host memory, this instance provides cost-effective throughput for GPU-driven virtual workstations, remote rendering, lightweight video transcoding, and parallel inference tasks that rely on external block storage.
